title: Florida House, District 89
what_it_does: Represents District 89 (Part of Palm Beach) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.

candidates.name: Cathy Higgins
candidates.occupation: Co-owner of two local businesses; former Mayor and council member, City of Atlantis
candidates.background: Cathy Higgins was born in West Palm Beach and raised in Lake Worth. She served 12 years on the Atlantis City Council, three of them as the city's first woman mayor, and she and her husband run two local businesses that employ close to 400 people. She built a dance program at The King's Academy and won the August 2026 Republican primary with about 67 percent.

candidates.name: Debra Tendrich
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Nonprofit founder and executive director; state representative since 2024
candidates.background: Debra Tendrich of Lake Worth is the founder and executive director of a nutrition-focused nonprofit and was elected to the Florida House in November 2024. In her first term she was the prime author of a domestic-violence protections law that passed both chambers unanimously, and she serves on the House Select Committee on Property Taxes.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted no on HJR 1-F (June 2, 2026 special session), which put a $250,000 non-school homestead exemption on the November 2026 ballot, and no on HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026), which would have phased out non-school homestead property taxes.

immigration.summary: Voted no on SB 2-C (Feb. 13, 2025), which created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, funded state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and added criminal penalties tied to immigration status.

sources.title: Florida House floor vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), 2025 Special Session C, third reading

housing.summary: Supports fully funding the state and local affordable-housing trust funds, expanding rental assistance and down-payment help, and faster permitting and redevelopment to add supply.
housing.quote: I support fully funding Florida’s state and local affordable housing trust funds, strengthening SHIP and SAIL to build and preserve affordable housing, expanding rental assistance, and increasing down-payment and closing-cost assistance for first-time homebuyers.

sources.title: VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters), State Representative 89: Debra Tendrich responses

abortion.summary: Supports abortion access particularly in cases of rape or incest, severe or fatal fetal abnormality, or a threat to the woman's physical or mental health, and says these decisions belong to a woman and her doctor.
abortion.quote: These are deeply personal and often difficult decisions that should be made by a woman and her doctor, informed by her faith and family if she chooses.

sources.title: VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters), State Representative 89: Debra Tendrich responses

growth.summary: Says Florida has often gone too far in preempting local governments and that local control over growth, development and flooding should be the default.
growth.quote: Home rule should be protected, and local control should be the default unless there is a clear and compelling statewide reason to intervene.

sources.title: VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters), State Representative 89: Debra Tendrich responses

healthcare.summary: Supports pursuing every available federal waiver and funding to keep Floridians covered and protecting Medicaid access for vulnerable groups; she does not explicitly call for Medicaid expansion.
healthcare.quote: As federal subsidies decline, I support pursuing every available federal waiver and funding opportunity to help Florida families maintain coverage while maximizing federal dollars and controlling state costs.

sources.title: VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters), State Representative 89: Debra Tendrich responses

elections.summary: Voted no on CS/CS/HB 991 when it passed the House on Feb. 25, 2026 and no on final House passage March 12, 2026. CS/CS/HB 991 (2026), now law (Ch. 2026-26), requires the state to verify voters' U.S. citizenship using driver-license and other government records and removes student and retirement-home IDs from the IDs accepted at the polls. On VOTE411 she said eligibility should be verified without making eligible voters go through a costly or complicated process.
elections.quote: Election integrity and voter access should work together.

other_issues.title: Named 2026 Legislator of the Year by the Florida Hispanic American Chamber of Commerce
other_issues.summary: Tendrich was named 2026 Legislator of the Year by the Florida Hispanic American Chamber of Commerce, which cited her support for Hispanic culture and businesses. Her campaign also announced endorsements from Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores, School Board member Virginia Savietto, Greenacres Council member Susy Diaz, Boca Raton Council member Yvette Drucker and Belle Glade Council member Joaquin Almazan.

record.item: Voted against CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; because the vote sent the question to voters rather than cutting taxes itself, a vote for it is coded as leaning toward sharply reducing homestead property taxes rather than as full agreement.
